Absolute criteria
• Demonstration of cysticerci by histologic or microscopic examination of a biopsy taken from the
brain or spinal cord lesion.
• Visualization of the parasite in the eye by funduscopy
• Neuroradiologic demonstration of cystic lesions containing a characteristic scolex

stem: Neuroimaging criteria
stem_raw:
Neuroimaging criteria
• Major neuroimaging criteria: Cystic lesions without a discernible scolex, multilobulated cystic
lesions in the subarachnoid space, typical small enhancing lesions, typical parenchymal brain
calcifications
• Confirmative neuroimaging criteria: Resolution of cystic lesions spontaneously or after cysticidal
drug therapy and migration of ventricular cysts documented on sequential neuroimaging studies
• Minor neuroimaging criteria: Obstructive hydrocephalus or abnormal enhancement of basal
leptomeninges

stem: Clinical/exposure criteria
stem_raw:
Clinical/exposure criteria
• Major clinical/exposure criteria: Demonstration of antibodies to cysticerci or cysticerci antigen in
cerebrospinal fluid by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay; Household contact with an individual
infected with T. solium; Evidence of cysticercosis outside the central nervous system (e.g.,
cigar-shaped soft-tissue calcifications)
• Minor clinical/exposure criteria: Clinical manifestations suggestive of neurocysticercosis;
Residence in a cysticercosis-endemic area; Frequent travel to a cysticercosis-endemic area
Diagnosis is confirmed by:
• One absolute criterion
• Two major neuroimaging criteria plus any clinical/exposure criteria
• One major and one confirmative neuroimaging criterion plus any clinical/exposure criteria
• One major neuroimaging criteria plus two clinical/exposure criteria (including at least one major
clinical/exposure criterion), with the exclusion of other pathologies producing similar
neuroimaging findings
A probable diagnosis is supported by the fulfillment of
• One major neuroimaging criterion plus any two clinical/exposure criteria
• One minor neuroimaging criterion plus at least one major clinical/exposure criterion
Other options: The MRI labeled as A shows ventriculomegaly in brain atrophy.

Detailed Explanations
Solution to Question 1:
The correct statement is that the CT score of water is 0. 
On CT, each image consists of a matrix of data points (pixels) that are assigned a number that
represents the X-ray attenuation(µ) at that point in the body. CT number is a scaled version of µ
that is normalised to the X-ray attenuation of water (µW).
CT = 1000 × (µ/µW − 1)
The resulting numbers are called ‘Hounsfield units’(HU). Due to this normalisation, water is
assigned 0 HU, and air is assigned a CT number of −1000 HU.
CT numbers:
• Water = 0 HU
• Solid soft tissues are centred around 0 HU
• Lungs = -1000 HU
